advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Restrict the `orphaned` set in `_recover_from_invalid_object` to entries dropped by `read-tree HEAD` (staged-but-not-in-HEAD), not the full `ls-files --cached` tracked set, before logging orphaned_worktree_paths.
evidence: 705:    """Paths currently staged in the index. ``ls-files --cached`` reads ``.git/index``
758:    # An orphan is an EARLIER failed write's file dropped from the index by the reset but left
759:    # in the worktree — visible to local replay yet uncommitted/unpushed.

`git ls-files --cached` lists the full index, i.e. every tracked file, the vast majority of which ARE committed at HEAD and are NOT orphaned after `read-tree HEAD`; only entries absent from HEAD are genuinely orphaned.
advisory.finding: In `_recover_from_invalid_object`, the `orphaned` set is `set(staged_before) - set(event_relpaths)`, but `staged_before` comes from `git ls-files --cached` which lists ALL tracked files (including files already committed at HEAD that survive `read-tree HEAD`), not only staged-but-uncommitted entries. The WARNING therefore reports every previously-committed tracked file as an `orphaned_worktree_path`, over-reporting the true orphan set (the uncommitted entries dropped by the reset).
scenarios: A real tracker with many committed event files hits a poisoned-index heal: the WARNING log lists the entire tracked-file set as orphaned_worktree_paths, obscuring the one genuine orphan and any real local↔remote divergence.
advisory.suggested_fix: Compute the orphan candidates as index entries NOT present at HEAD (e.g. diff `git ls-files --cached` against `git ls-tree -r --name-only HEAD`, or capture staged-but-uncommitted paths via `git diff --cached --name-only HEAD`), then subtract `event_relpaths`.

All four new poison/recovery tests drive stage_and_commit (single-event path, calling _recover_from_invalid_object with [relative_path]); the batch call site (passing relpaths) is separate wiring that could regress — wrong arguments, branch never reached, or heal/rollback ordering — with no test going red.
